_comment: Cross-boundary architecture manifest (#124; governance PIPELINE_GOVERNANCE_AND_STATE §10). The DECLARED ground truth for the couplings NO import tool sees — external-process invocations, cross-language dispatch, guarded entry points, and client<->server rule boundaries. tests/test_arch_manifest.py asserts the real code matches this manifest; a NEW undeclared edge (program OR caller) FAILS the suite. This complements import-linter (intra-Python) + dependency-cruiser (intra-Node), which see imports only. Update this file DELIBERATELY when you add such an edge — that edit is the review surface for a new cross-boundary coupling. HONEST LIMITS (#206 review): the detectors are static heuristics — an argv assembled dynamically (a helper-built list, string concatenation) or dispatched through an unlisted runner name is invisible to the scan (the research doc's conclusion: these are semantic couplings only a declared manifest + convention can cover), and the guard check is syntactic presence, not runtime reachability (dead code containing the call still passes — vulture's domain).

scan._comment: The scan scope for the external-program fitness functions (#206 review — the scope was previously implicit and acquisition-only, silently missing scripts/ callers of declared programs). data/ is excluded deliberately: it holds stored artifacts + archived spikes (e.g. benchmark_results/*/run_spike.py), not live code. tests/ is excluded (the scanner + fixtures would self-trigger).

external_programs._comment: Every external program the live Python trees shell out to (argv[0] of a subprocess argv-list, whether via subprocess.* directly or an injectable runner seam). BOTH directions are enforced: an undeclared program fails, and an undeclared CALLER of a declared program fails (callers lists are load-bearing, not documentation).

claude.why: Stage 2 Wave-2 discovery — `claude -p` print mode with WebSearch (the speculative residual index); plus the Stage-2 CLI reliability/smoke harnesses.

node.why: Stage 3 capture — Python->Node Playwright dispatch (the cross-LANGUAGE edge).

pdftotext.why: PDF -> layout text (poppler). Stage 4 harvest + Stage 5 handbook page slice + the manual-enrichment importer.

pdftoppm.why: PDF -> raster PNG for OCR (poppler). Stage 4.

pdfinfo.why: PDF page count (poppler). Stage 5 handbook slice sizing.

docker.why: LCT-DB side: pipe SQL into the lct_postgres container (the Docker-required rule).

docker-compose.why: LCT-DB side: container lifecycle for the import-to-docker flow.

python3.why: rebuild_database.py re-invokes sibling scripts as subprocesses.

entry_point_guards._comment: An invariant guard that MUST be reached by every listed entry point — the fix for the class of bug where a rule is enforced at one entry point but a sibling skips it. #198 review finding #2 (headless CLIs) + #206 review (the OLDER per-district CLIs were still unguarded). The console inherits these guards by calling the same run_batch functions (server.py has no parallel implementation). Batch-grain: whole-batch runners + the Stage-2 legacy CLI.
entry_point_guards.why: #168: never run a pipeline stage on a terminal `abandoned` batch (its schools are excluded from the attempted-set; running it re-queues them — the #162 poison).

entry_point_guards._comment: District-grain twin (#206 review): the Stage-3/4 legacy CLIs (finish/reconstruct/run) take a district dir, not a batch — the dir's discovery.json records the producing batch, and assert_district_runnable refuses if THAT batch is abandoned.
entry_point_guards.why: #168: the per-district CLI recovery/write ops must not resurrect a district whose artifacts belong to a terminal abandoned batch.

client_server_boundaries._comment: Rules about the browser-JS <-> server boundary — a class the import graphs can't see at all. Scans are RECURSIVE over the scope dir and whole-file (multi-line safe), #206 review.

forbidden_client_comparisons._comment: A server-authoritative rule literal must NOT be re-decided in client JS (it duplicates a server truth and drifts). #198 review finding #3: the gate@6 benchmark badge keyed on `c.batch_id === 'batch_00000'` instead of the server-computed `is_benchmark` (batch_type='benchmark'). Flagged forms (#206 review widened these): (in)equality comparisons, .includes/.startsWith/.endsWith predicates, switch-case labels, and assigning the literal to a variable (the indirection vector). A purely-display template string (`benchmark-walled (batch_00000)`) is allowed.
forbidden_client_comparisons.use_instead: the server-computed `is_benchmark` field on the candidates payload (batch_type='benchmark')

single_definition_helpers._comment: A shared client helper must be defined in exactly ONE file (common.js) so its behavior can't fork across the stage views. #198 review finding #5. Detected forms (#206 review widened): function/const/let/var definitions AND property assignments (window.LCT.name = / LCT.name =). A behavioral duplicate under a DIFFERENT name is beyond static reach — that's what review + the shared-helper convention are for.
single_definition_helpers.name: statusBadge

file_dispatches._comment: The file-based stage handoffs — regenerable, auditable RECEIPTS (the DB is the working store; governance §1). Declared here for provenance; test_file_dispatch_producers_reference_artifact asserts each producer module actually references its artifact filename (a light contract that the declared producer is the real one). NOT the transport between stages.

receipts.role: per-district full per-school discovery audit trail

shared_config._comment: #205 part 1 (governance §10): the config-as-data knobs are a CROSS-LANGUAGE edge — Python reads them via common/config_loader.py, Node reads the same JSON natively (capture_discovery.mjs), so a malformed/renamed key fails a stage at runtime, invisible to every import tool. Each knob file is declared here with its JSON Schema (under schemas_dir); tests/test_config_schemas.py validates every file against its schema AND enforces coverage both ways (an undeclared knob file fails; a declared-but-missing file fails). Adding a knob = add the file, its schema (or reuse a shape schema), and this declaration — the declaration is the review surface. Part 2 of #205 (datacontract-cli on the stage receipt artifacts above) is deferred until #478 stabilizes the Stage 8 artifacts.
